title: Derived change of rings along a map of ring sheaves is left adjoint to restriction of scalars, with normalized unit and transposes
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\varphi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Use the abelian categories of sheaves of $\mathcal O$- and $\mathcal O'$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal O)$, $D(\mathcal O')$ with localizations $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and the change of rings $-\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ is exact, so applying it termwise defines $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi:D(\mathcal O')\to D(\mathcal O)$. Let $L\varphi^*=-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O':D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O')$ be the derived change of rings of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], computed on K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, lem-pc-kflat-resolution] through the canonical isomorphism $c_P:L\varphi^*(QP)\cong Q(P\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O')$. Then $L\varphi^*$ is left adjoint to $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$: there are bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O')}(L\varphi^*K,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(K,\operatorname{Res}_\varphi H),$$
natural in $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ and $H\in D(\mathcal O')$, normalized on representatives as follows. Let $P$ be a K-flat complex of $\mathcal O$-modules with flat terms. (1) Under $c_P$, the unit at $QP$ is the class of the termwise map $P\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(P\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O')$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. (2) For a complex $H$ of $\mathcal O'$-modules and a morphism of complexes $g:P\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi H$, the adjunct of $Q(g)$ is, under $c_P$, the class of the morphism of complexes $P\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'\to H$, $x\otimes a\mapsto a\,g(x)$. In particular, if $g$ is a quasi-isomorphism, the counit at $QH$ is this class composed with $c_P$ and the inverse of $L\varphi^*(Q(g))$. No flatness of $\varphi$ and no boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O$, $S=\mathcal O'$ and let the topos of sheaves on $\mathcal C$ be the same on both sides. Applying the ringed-topos module adjunction to the identity geometric morphism and the ring map $\varphi:R\to S$ gives an underived adjunction $G\dashv F$, where $G(N)=N\otimes_R S$ and $F=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$. The Hom maps are the balanced formulas $v\mapsto(x\mapsto v(x\otimes1))$ and $w\mapsto(x\otimes a\mapsto a\,w(x))$; they commute with restrictions and sheafification, and the triangle identities hold on pure tensors.

Restriction of scalars leaves the underlying sheaf of abelian groups and all morphisms unchanged. Kernels in the module-sheaf category are sectionwise, while cokernels are sheafifications of sectionwise cokernels; restricting the scalar action therefore preserves both kernels and cokernels. Hence $F$ is exact, with no flatness assumption on $\varphi$.

The exact-functor derived factorization and derived-functor theorem apply to $F$: its termwise functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms and identifies the everywhere-defined right derived functor with termwise restriction. Thus the derived functor is the stated $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ on unbounded derived categories. By the derived-change-of-rings node, the tensor functor has an everywhere-defined left derived functor $LG=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$, and a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ computes it as $Q(P\otimes_R S)$; such flat-term K-flat resolutions exist by the cited resolution theorem. The canonical comparison $c_P$ is independent of the chosen resolution.

proof.text: Apply the general derived-adjoint-functors theorem to the underived pair $G\dashv F$ of Step 1. Step 2 makes $RF$ everywhere defined, and Step 3 makes $LG$ everywhere defined, so the theorem supplies a canonical bifunctorial bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(S)}(LG(K),H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,RF(H))$. Substituting the identifications from Step 3 gives exactly the displayed bijection with $RF=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ and $LG=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$.

Let $P$ be a flat-term K-flat complex of $R$-modules. In the explicit pre-derived Hom formula take $M=P$, target complex $K=G(P)$, $s=\mathrm{id}_{G(P)}$, $t=\mathrm{id}_P$, and $f=\eta_P:P\to F G(P)$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Since $F$ is exact, the right-derived comparison $p_s$ is the identity after the identification of Step 3; since $P$ computes $LG$, the left-derived comparison $u_t$ is $c_P$. The homotopy adjunct $a_h(f)$ is $\mathrm{id}_{G(P)}$ by the termwise adjunction. Thus the formula sends $Q(\eta_P)$ to $c_P:LG(QP)\to QG(P)$. Equivalently, under the identification $c_P$ the identity of $LG(QP)$ corresponds to $Q(\eta_P)$, which is exactly the asserted unit.

Let $g:P\to F(H)$ be a chain map as in the statement. Its termwise adjunct is $\widetilde g:P\otimes_R S\to H$, $x\otimes a\mapsto a\,g(x)$: $R$-balancedness makes this well defined on the presheaf tensor and hence on its sheafification, and $d_H(a\,g(x))=a\,g(d_Px)$ makes it a chain map. Apply the cited fraction formula with $M=P$, $K=H$, $s=\mathrm{id}_H$, $t=\mathrm{id}_P$, and $f=g$. Its two comparison maps are again $p_s=\mathrm{id}$ and $u_t=c_P$, so the derived adjunct is $Q(\widetilde g)\circ c_P$. If $g$ is a quasi-isomorphism, write $q=Q(g):QP\xrightarrow{\sim}F(QH)$. Naturality of the adjunction in its first variable gives $\varepsilon_{QH}\circ LG(q)=Q(\widetilde g)\circ c_P$, since $\varepsilon_{QH}$ is the adjunct of $\mathrm{id}_{F(QH)}$. The functor $LG$ carries the isomorphism $q$ to an isomorphism; composing with its inverse gives $\varepsilon_{QH}=Q(\widetilde g)\circ c_P\circ LG(q)^{-1}$, the claimed counit formula. No flatness of the ring map or boundedness has been used.
